parameters: \>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>In the event that you are attacked, a combat encounter will ensue.
\>Your opponents will be placed on the left, and your allies on the right.
\>You can view allies' HP (Health Points) and SP (Skill Points) in the bottom.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>In menus you can use the arrow keys to move the cursor, [ENTER] to
\>select the highlighted option, and [ESC] to go back.
\>You can also use the mouse, and click options to select them.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>If you are playing on a touch screen, tap options to select them and
\>press the Back button to go back.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>You can also go back in the command screen to enter the party screen,
\>which will allow you to adjust your settings and/or attempt to flee
\>from battle.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>Try using a \C[17]basic attack\C[0] on the enemy.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>Excellent. Basic attacks deal damage according to your weapon and
\>Ferocity stat, which can be observed in the Analysis screen.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>Another method of dealing damage is through certain \C[17]Skills\C[0]. These are
\>abilities of your allies' Manifestations, and are the meat of combat
\>as a whole.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>Try using an \C[17]Elemental skill\C[0] on the enemy.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>Excellent. With your elemental attack, you struck the enemy's \C[17]weakness\C[0].
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>Allies and enemies alike possess different \C[17]affinities\C[0] for different
\>damage types. Among these are \C[17]weaknesses\C[0] and \C[17]resistances\C[0].
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>Striking a \C[17]weakness\C[0] deals double damage and knocks down the target,
\>granting you another action and causing them to lose their next action.
\>Striking a \C[17]resistance\C[0] inflicts half the normal damage.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>\C[17]Physical attacks\C[0] can also land \C[17]Critical\C[0] hits. This causes the attack to act
\>as if the target was weak to that damage type, even if they aren't.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>You can also use many consumable items you obtain from the \C[17]Items\C[0] screen.
\>This applies in combat, where it will take an action, and out of combat.
\>Outside combat, the items screen can be found in the pause menu.
\>\C[7]System\C[0]
\>The \C[17]Rush\C[0] command is a way to speed up fights you aren't concerned about
\>losing. During Rush, the party will automatically use their basic attacks
\>and animations will be sped up. It can be ended by pressing [ESC].
\>Rush command is broken as of v0.3 and makes party members use
\>skills instead of just their basic attacks.
\>While this would normally be a good thing in most other games,
\>the brain of RPGMaker's autobattle AI was seemingly scrubbed with
\>a mixture of bleach and pop rocks, judging by their intelligence.
